$doc.what: Engine capability matrix: authored config; no dedicated verification runs.
$doc.contract: PRD §2 Engine entity: id, name, lane, payload, price + capability flags mask / seed / imageRef / styleRef / maxResolution / tokenLimit. Every flag carries a verification state. A 3D engine also declares `verbs`: the steps it serves (law 16).
semantics: value = what the product lets you do with this engine today (committed graphs and routes), not what the model could do in principle.
state=verified: the value was observed (seen working in real use or smoke). For value=false, verified means the absence is a structural fact (no committed graph or route), not a probed model limit.
state=unverified: authored belief from model docs or preset ceilings, not yet observed. Shown as unverified, never guessed better (law 12).
note: plain-words badge text (law 12), curated static copy, never generated.
Numeric flags may be null = unknown or not applicable (the note says which). Unknown beats a confident wrong number.
Flags flip as usage proves them: update value/state here with dated evidence when real use observes something new.

verbs: which 3D steps this engine serves (law 16). The surfaces read it to badge a verb an engine does not do rather than hide the engine (law 12). An image engine has no verbs list: the image lane's steps are presets, not engine-declared. The RUNNER is the authority (tools/3d/runner.py KINDS) and cockpit/server/app/mesh.py MESH_KINDS is its server-side mirror; this list is the published copy, and a test holds the three in agreement (test_mesh.py).

params: the handles a SURFACE may offer for a verb, keyed by verb then by the runner's own param name. It is a published OFFER, not the runner's whitelist: the runner accepts more than this (a knob it takes but the product does not offer is simply absent here), so the guard is `published ⊆ runner` and never equality. A key here that the runner would refuse by name is the drift the test catches. A mesh engine has one because its handles are engine-declared; an image engine's live in presets/*.json `inputs` instead, which is why no image row carries this key.

params[verb][key]: `label` is the artist's name for it, `effect` the permanently visible plain-effect line (never a tooltip), `type`/`choices`/`default` the control. `state` is the knob's own verification (law 12), read the same way a capability's is: verified = this range was run and measured, unverified = authored from the engine's docs and not yet exercised. `supported: false` publishes a handle this engine does NOT have, with `why`: the surface lists it and dashes it rather than leaving an artist to wonder whether the app forgot it (law 12: badge, never filter). Seed is NOT here: it is a run-level field, published as the `seed` capability above.

audio rows (payload audio) name their `provider`, the adapter that reaches them (elevenlabs or voice-runner), and `enabled`. Per verb they declare `models`, `params` (public controls), `fixed` provider fields, `tariffs` ({unit, micro_usd, measure, source, read_on}: exact integer micro-dollars, where measure names the text or control the unit counts), `takes_per_attempt`, and optional `text_limits`. `voice_providers` limits speech to voices designed or saved at those providers. `terms` records the provider's terms on its outputs: every take carries them, and a hop they forbid is badged with their reason (laws 12, 21). The seed is published as the `seed` capability, as for 3D.

engines.name: TRELLIS.2 4B

pipeline_type.label: RESOLUTION TIER
pipeline_type.effect: How fine the grid is before the mesh is built. The cascade keeps small features the coarse pass rounds off; 512 is one pass and comes back sooner. Measured on one RTX 4090: 64 s against 46 s, and it is the bake that costs, not the sampling. It barely changes the triangle count; that budget is the extraction's.
pipeline_type.evidence: bench 2026-08-30: 512 → 45.8 s, 928,007 tris, 616,775 verts; 1024_cascade → 63.9 s, 963,650 tris, 707,220 verts. The tier's effect lands in vertices, not faces.

texture_size.label: TEXTURE SIZE
texture_size.effect: The PBR set is baked at this size. 1024 and 2048 cost the same; 4096 adds about 18 s to the bake and a few megabytes to the file. Take 4096 for a hero prop the camera gets close to, 1024 when it is going into a crowd.
texture_size.evidence: bench 2026-08-30: extraction 43.9 / 38.2 / 56.3 s and 33.6 / 34.8 / 39.1 MB at 1024 / 2048 / 4096. The low two differ by less than the run-to-run spread. On an RTX 4090, going from 2048 to 4096 costs +47% in extraction time, not 2×.

engines.price: free: local GPU time; cost reads in minutes, not seconds
engines.note: Serves DECIMATE by RE-EXTRACTION, not by simplifying: a take keeps its voxel field, and this re-runs the bake at another triangle count (a fresh remesh, unwrap and texture bake rather than a collapse of the finished GLB). It has no seam floor, so it is the only route below gltfpack's, and it re-bakes the texture at a size of your choosing. Only its OWN takes, and only those that kept a field set. Measured 2026-08-29 on a 931,981-triangle lantern: 30,000 asked landed 28,007 in 14 s, where gltfpack on the same mesh floored at 362,918. Keeping the field costs the take a sidecar of 21-92 MB (per prop, sized by occupied voxels); the tray states it and purge frees it.

seed.evidence: funnel.py sends a fixed seed (424242) on every run; end-to-end green twice
seed.note: Seed accepted per run; the funnel always sends the same one, so variety and reproducibility are unexercised.

imageRef.evidence: image→mesh proven end-to-end twice via funnel.py
imageRef.note: The image is the input — image-conditioned mesh generation.

styleRef.note: No style channel in the funnel path.

maxResolution.note: Not applicable — output is a mesh (GLB); the pipeline conditions from a fixed input crop.

tokenLimit.note: Not applicable — image-conditioned in the funnel path; no text channel wired.

engines.name: Hunyuan3D 2.1

octree_resolution.label: RESOLUTION TIER
octree_resolution.effect: How finely the shape is sampled before it is turned into a surface. It does NOT give you more triangles — Paint rebuilds whatever it is given at 40,000, so every tier lands the same count and the same file size. What it changes is how true that surface is to the thin parts. It is the steepest handle here: measured, 512 costs about 39 s more than the default.
octree_resolution.evidence: bench 2026-08-30: shape generation 22.8 / 35.5 / 62.2 s at 256 / 384 / 512, and 40,000 triangles at 9.2 MB in all three. 512 also raises shape VRAM from 7.8 to 8.9 GB.

texture_size.label: TEXTURE SIZE
texture_size.why: Paint bakes its atlas at a size fixed inside the pipeline — there is no handle to turn. It also simplifies whatever it is given to 40,000 triangles and re-unwraps before painting, so the texture is sized to that, not to the mesh you asked for.

engines.price: free: local GPU time; cost reads in minutes, not seconds
engines.note: Shape + paint stages: textured mesh output, with the full PBR set embedded (albedo + packed metallic/roughness). Serves TEXTURE on ANY mesh: Paint takes a mesh and a reference image and repaints it (shape locked, appearance branching). Honesty first: Paint simplifies its input to 40,000 faces and re-unwraps before painting (upstream's own hard default), so the textured child carries Paint's topology and UVs, never its parent's. The child's facts line prints its own count. Measured 2026-08-30 on a 970,535-triangle TRELLIS.2 mesh: the 40k path paints in 51 s (66 s stage wall, 13.7 GB peak); skipping the simplify at native density burned 45+ CPU-minutes without reaching the bake and is not offered. Deterministic: Paint hard-seeds its diffusion, so the same mesh and the same reference give the same child; one take, like decimate.

seed.evidence: funnel.py sends a fixed seed (424242) on every run; end-to-end green twice
seed.note: Seed accepted per run; the funnel always sends the same one, so variety and reproducibility are unexercised.

imageRef.evidence: image→mesh proven end-to-end twice via funnel.py
imageRef.note: The image is the input — image-conditioned mesh generation.

styleRef.note: No style channel in the funnel path.

maxResolution.note: Not applicable — output is a mesh (GLB); the pipeline conditions from a fixed input crop.

tokenLimit.note: Not applicable — image-conditioned in the funnel path; no text channel wired.

engines.name: gltfpack (meshopt)
engines.price: free — local CPU; 0.8 s on a 970k-triangle mesh (measured 2026-08-29), not the minutes a generator costs
engines.note: A classic tool, not a model (law 16): meshoptimizer's simplifier over a GLB. It serves DECIMATE only (mesh in, smaller mesh out) and never generates. The triangle target is a request the mesh may refuse: a machine UV atlas locks the seams a simplifier would have to collapse, so a TRELLIS.2 mesh floors at ~8–10% of its source triangles. The child states the count it actually reached.

mask.note: Not meaningful — the input is a mesh, not a picture.

seed.evidence: tools/3d/runner.py declares the decimate kind seedless and refuses a seed by name; the run route sends none
seed.note: Deterministic — the same mesh and the same triangle target give the same child every time, so no seed is recorded rather than one that did nothing.

imageRef.note: The input is a mesh; there is no image channel.

styleRef.note: No style channel — this tool changes topology, never appearance.

maxResolution.note: Not applicable — the output is a mesh (GLB).
